section: International trade - patterns, trade blocs, chokepoints; India's export and import composition
subsections: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)
Major ports of India → state and coast

accepted.s: Which one of the following agreements provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports, with Indian exports rising by 12% in its first year?
accepted.x: The India-UAE CEPA, signed in 2022, provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports and exports rose by 12% in the first year.
accepted.tq: Use the agreement-specific numerical feature to separate closely related trade agreements.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India-Australia trade agreements:
1. The India-Australia ECTA was signed in December 2022.
2. A CECA between India and Australia is still being negotiated.
3. The ECTA was signed in March 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The India-Australia ECTA was signed in December 2022, while a broader CECA is still under negotiation. March 2024 refers to the India-EFTA TEPA, not the Australia agreement.
accepted.tq: Separate the agreement date from the date of a neighbouring agreement and identify the false statement.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the European Free Trade Association involved in the India-EFTA TEPA?
accepted.x: The India-EFTA TEPA involves Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. Austria is not listed among the EFTA members in the agreement.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a four-member regional grouping.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: The India-EFTA TEPA is associated with which one of the following commitments?
o: Tariff reduction on over 90% of goods by the European Union
Opening of 137 service sub-sectors by the United Kingdom
Binding investment of US$100 billion over 15 years
Duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports in the first year
accepted.x: The India-EFTA TEPA contains a binding commitment of US$100 billion investment over 15 years. The other options refer to the India-UAE CEPA, India-UK CETA and India-EU FTA respectively.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive financial commitment with the correct agreement.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: The India-EFTA TEPA came into force in which year?
accepted.x: The India-EFTA TEPA has been in force since 2025. March 2024 is associated with its signing or key agreement milestone, not its enforcement year.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the signing year from the year in which an agreement came into force.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India-UK CETA — Signed in July 2025 and services-focused
India-Oman CEPA — In force from 1 June 2025
India-New Zealand FTA — Signed in April 2025
India-EU FTA — Ratification completed in January 2026
accepted.x: The India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025 and is services-focused. The India-Oman CEPA came into force on 1 June 2026, the India-New Zealand FTA was signed in April 2026, and the India-EU FTA remained pending ratification and signing.
accepted.tq: Check the agreement against both its date and its distinctive subject matter.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s:
With reference to recent Indian trade agreements, consider the following statements:
1. The India-Oman CEPA came into force on 1 June 2026.
2. The India-New Zealand FTA was signed in April 2026.
3. The India-EU FTA negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026.
4. Ratification and signing of the India-EU FTA were pending in 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The India-Oman CEPA took effect on 1 June 2026, the India-New Zealand FTA was signed in April 2026, and the India-EU negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026 while formal ratification and signing remained pending.
accepted.tq: Use a comprehensive coded option when all dated statements belong to the same current-affairs cluster.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: The India-EU FTA, described as the “Mother of All Deals”, provides access on approximately what proportion of tariff lines?
accepted.x: The India-EU FTA provides access on 97% of tariff lines. The 99.5% figure refers to the proportion of trade value covered, not tariff lines.
accepted.tq: Separate tariff-line coverage from trade-value coverage when two percentages appear together.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the India-UK CETA?
o: It came into force on 1 June 2026.
It binds US$100 billion investment over 15 years.
The United Kingdom opens 137 service sub-sectors.
It provides access on 97% of tariff lines and 99.5% of trade value.
accepted.x: The India-UK CETA involves the United Kingdom opening 137 service sub-sectors. The other statements refer to the India-EU FTA, India-EFTA TEPA and India-Oman CEPA respectively.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise sectoral concession rather than the agreement’s general label.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: In the last three years, India concluded FTAs covering how many countries and providing zero-duty access to markets accounting for approximately what share of world GDP?
accepted.x: India concluded nine FTAs covering 38 countries, providing zero-duty access to markets that account for about 70% of world GDP.
accepted.tq: Pair the count of countries with the corresponding percentage rather than interchanging the figures.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which of the following reviews were ongoing in relation to India’s trade agreements?
o: India-Australia ECTA and India-New Zealand FTA
accepted.x: Reviews of the India-ASEAN FTA and the India-Korea CEPA were ongoing. The other agreements were not identified as the agreements under review.
accepted.tq: Match the review process with the correct pair of existing agreements.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s external trade in FY26:
1. Merchandise exports were US$441.78 billion.
2. Merchandise imports were US$775 billion.
3. The merchandise trade deficit was US$333.2 billion.
4. Goods and services exports were US$860.09 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four figures are correct for FY26: merchandise exports of US$441.78 billion, imports of US$775 billion, a trade deficit of US$333.2 billion and goods-plus-services exports of US$860.09 billion.
accepted.tq: Retain each figure separately and select the coded option containing the complete set.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s merchandise export and import growth in FY26?
o: Exports increased by 0.93% and imports by 7.45%.
Exports declined by 0.93% and imports increased by 7.45%.
Exports increased by 4.22% and imports by 0.93%.
Exports increased by 7.45% and imports by 0.93%.
accepted.x: FY26 merchandise exports rose by 0.93%, while merchandise imports rose by 7.45%. The 4.22% figure relates to growth in goods and services exports.
accepted.tq: Compare the direction and percentage of change instead of confusing merchandise figures with combined exports.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which side of India’s external account was reported as being in surplus?
accepted.x: Services were the surplus side of the account, whereas merchandise trade recorded a substantial deficit.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison between goods and services to identify the surplus component.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: At the time a trade deal with the United States was still under negotiation, the US tariff in force was stated as:
accepted.x: A US tariff of 25% plus 25%, amounting to 50%, was in force while the deal remained under negotiation.
accepted.tq: Add the two stated tariff components and avoid selecting only the combined figure.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with WTO MC14 held at Yaounde, Cameroon?
o: E-commerce customs moratorium — Lapsed on 31 March 2026
accepted.x: The e-commerce customs moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026. No permanent solution was reached on public stockholding, no Phase-2 fisheries subsidies deal was concluded, and the Appellate Body remained paralysed.
accepted.tq: Find the single correctly matched outcome among several reversed WTO developments.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: WTO MC14 was held during which period and at which place?
accepted.x: The 14th WTO Ministerial Conference was held at Yaounde, Cameroon, from 26 to 29 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Combine the venue and dates to distinguish a multilateral trade conference from other events.
accepted.sec: Free trade agreements of India (India-UAE CEPA, India-Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA)

accepted.s: India has how many major ports and approximately how many non-major ports?
o: 13 major ports and about 200 non-major ports
accepted.x: India has 13 major ports and about 200 non-major ports. Twelve major ports are operational, but the approved total is now 13.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total number of major ports from the number currently operational.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India’s ports is correct?
o: Non-major ports are governed exclusively by the Major Port Authorities Act.
All ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act.
Major ports are governed by State Maritime Boards, while non-major ports are governed by the Union Government.
Major ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act, while non-major ports fall under State Maritime Boards.
accepted.x: The 13 major ports are governed by the Major Port Authorities Act, while about 200 non-major ports are administered under State Maritime Boards.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority would administer a port by separating major and non-major categories.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Vadhavan Port, approved on 19 June 2024, is located in which district and State?
accepted.x: Vadhavan is a greenfield deep-draft port located in Palghar district of Maharashtra. It was approved on 19 June 2024.
accepted.tq: Match the newly approved port with its specific district and State.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the ownership structure and estimated cost of Vadhavan Port?
o: JNPA 50% and Maharashtra Maritime Board 50%, costing about ₹76,220 crore
JNPA 74% and Maharashtra Maritime Board 26%, costing about ₹7,622 crore
JNPA 26% and Maharashtra Maritime Board 74%, costing about ₹7,622 crore
JNPA 74% and Maharashtra Maritime Board 26%, costing about ₹76,220 crore
accepted.x: Vadhavan Port is being developed through an SPV in which JNPA holds 74% and the Maharashtra Maritime Board 26%; the estimated cost is about ₹76,220 crore.
accepted.tq: Match both ownership percentages and project cost without reversing the partners.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The target year for the completion of Vadhavan Port is:
accepted.x: Vadhavan Port has a target completion year of 2034.
accepted.tq: Use the project timeline as the decisive fact among nearby future years.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Deendayal Port — Gujarat, Gulf of Kachchh, west coast
Kochi Port — Tamil Nadu, east coast
Paradip Port — Andhra Pradesh, east coast
accepted.x: Deendayal Port is in Gujarat on the Gulf of Kachchh on the west coast. Mumbai is in Maharashtra, Kochi is in Kerala, and Paradip is in Odisha.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure port-State-coast pair and eliminate reversed locations.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which major port is a tidal port and was associated with a Free Trade Zone and Asia’s first Export Processing Zone established in 1965?
accepted.x: Deendayal Port at Kandla is a tidal port in the Gulf of Kachchh and is associated with a Free Trade Zone and Asia’s first EPZ in 1965.
accepted.tq: Identify the port through its distinctive historical and functional features.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mumbai Port is a natural harbour on Salsette Island.
2. Jawaharlal Nehru Port was built to decongest Mumbai Port.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru Port is India’s first 100% landlord major port.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mumbai is a natural harbour on Salsette Island, while Jawaharlal Nehru Port was developed to decongest it and became India’s first 100% landlord major port.
accepted.tq: Combine related features of neighbouring ports and select the complete correct set.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Jawaharlal Nehru Port?
o: Oldest artificial port of the east coast
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru Port, also known as Nhava Sheva, is India’s largest container port. The other descriptions refer to Chennai, Kolkata-Haldia and Visakhapatnam respectively.
accepted.tq: Match the port with its unique superlative or physical characteristic.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following ports from north to south along the Indian coastline:
A. Mumbai
B. Kochi
C. Deendayal
D. Mormugao
accepted.x: From north to south, the order is Deendayal, Mumbai, Mormugao and Kochi.
accepted.tq: Use geographical order rather than administrative location alone; identify the northernmost and southernmost ports first.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Mormugao Port is located in which State and is primarily associated with which cargo?
accepted.x: Mormugao is a major port of Goa associated with iron-ore cargo. It also recorded the fastest cargo growth in FY26 at 15.91%.
accepted.tq: Match the port with both its State and characteristic cargo.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kochi — Natural port on Vembanad Lake
Chennai — Natural harbour on Salsette Island
Visakhapatnam — Artificial all-weather harbour north of Adam’s Bridge
Tuticorin — Deepest landlocked port called the “Brightest Jewel”
accepted.x: Kochi is a natural port on Vembanad Lake. Salsette Island is associated with Mumbai, the artificial all-weather harbour north of Adam’s Bridge is Tuticorin, and the “Brightest Jewel” is Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Separate similar harbour descriptions by matching each physical feature to its port.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kamarajar — India’s first corporatised major port
V.O. Chidambaranar — Artificial all-weather deep-sea harbour north of Adam’s Bridge
Paradip — Oldest artificial port of the east coast
Chennai — Oldest artificial port of the east coast
accepted.x: Paradip is not the oldest artificial port of the east coast. Chennai has that distinction; Paradip is located in the Mahanadi delta and was commissioned in 1966.
accepted.tq: Find the port whose characteristic has been swapped with that of a nearby port.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Visakhapatnam Port is distinguished by which combination of features?
o: Deepest landlocked, protected port and known as the “Brightest Jewel”
Natural port on Vembanad Lake and the oldest major port
Only riverine major port and located on the Hooghly
Tidal port and Asia’s first EPZ
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked and protected port and is described as the “Brightest Jewel”. The other combinations describe Deendayal, Kolkata-Haldia and Kochi respectively.
accepted.tq: Select the combination containing the port’s two distinctive identifying features.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of port classification?
accepted.x: Quilon (Kollam) is a minor port, whereas Kochi, Mumbai and New Mangalore are major ports.
accepted.tq: Identify the single port belonging to a different administrative classification.
accepted.sec: Major ports of India → state and coast  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
